subject: Security gate dependency grid and MAP sequencing — Seastone Financial evaluation
messages:
From: Anya Novak <anya.novak@seastone.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: tom.rivers@seastone.com, procurement@seastone.com
Date: 2026-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Seastone evaluation — security/compliance asks and MAP kickoff

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. We're preparing the MAP for Seastone's evaluation and need to lock down the security/compliance gates in the next two weeks. High level asks from our side:

- SOC 2 scope & timeline (which controls are in-scope for hosted API vs private deployment)
- SIG/CAIQ gaps and expected evidence owners
- DPA redline status and data retention capabilities (EU residency, retention windows by data type)
- A clear dependency grid: what must be completed before we can start functional testing vs what can be parallelized

Can you share a short dependency grid and a proposed sequenced MAP (milestones, owners, and target dates)? We want to align with our security and procurement teams by EOD 10/15.

Also looping Tom (security) and procurement for initial visibility.

Thanks,
Anya
Director of Security Programs
Seastone Financial
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Anya Novak <anya.novak@seastone.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seastone evaluation — security/compliance asks and MAP kickoff

Anya — thanks, and great to meet Tom on the call. I've attached a first-pass "security dependency grid" (spreadsheet) and a short SOC 2 summary that maps our control coverage to hosted and private deployment modes. Key notes up front:

- SOC 2: our current Type II report covers hosted API for the controls typically requested by financial customers; private deployments require a scoped checklist (we support on-prem/VPC but the attestation falls to the customer for certain infrastructure controls). See tab "SOC2-scope" in the spreadsheet.
- SIG/CAIQ: we've pre-filled ~80% of the CAIQ; remaining items require cloud infra evidence or customer-specific network configs. Owner column included.
- DPA & retention: we support DPA redlines in most cases but will need to confirm EU data residency options if you require token-level residency. We can provide 3/7/10-year retention tiers by artifact type (transaction logs, user-profiles, debug traces).

High level sequencing I propose (draft):
1) Evidence intake & CAIQ completion (owner: Seastone security; Redwood SME: Kimberly) — target: 10/22
2) SOC 2 mapping & gap triage (owner: Redwood compliance / Kimberly) — target: 10/29
3) DPA finalization + legal redlines (owner: Seastone legal & Redwood legal) — target: 11/05
4) Staging evaluation (hosted) — functional tests + data residency validation (if required) — target: 11/12
5) Final acceptance window + roll to production (per MAP) — target: 11/19

I'm attaching: security-dependency-grid-v1.xlsx (contains owners, blockers, and which artifacts we can produce immediately) and redwood-soc2-summary.pdf.

Can you confirm which retention tiers you expect for each artifact type? Once we have that, Kim and I will fill the grid and lock milestone owners. If helpful, we can run a 30-minute evidence intake session on 10/13 or 10/14.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Manager, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachments: security-dependency-grid-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, Anya Novak <anya.novak@seastone.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-12T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seastone evaluation — sequencing notes (runtime & private)

Adding a couple of technical constraints we should reflect in the dependency grid:

- Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) takes longer due to network/firewall coordination and key management setup. Estimate: 4–6 weeks from signed ARO (we can shorten with pre-staged images and an infra runbook).
- Hosted evaluation (recommended first step) supports most SOC 2 evidence immediately and allows the functional test window while private setup proceeds.
- If Seastone requires EU residency for transaction logs specifically, we can route storage to our EU region but will need a config change and a short blackout for full export validation (~2 business days).

I recommend we mark "staging (hosted) evaluation" as a hard milestone before private cutover in the MAP to reduce overall time to test. Happy to join intake session and map infra owners.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
From: Anya Novak <anya.novak@seastone.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: tom.rivers@seastone.com, procurement@seastone.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-13T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seastone evaluation — security/compliance asks and MAP kickoff

Grace / team — thanks for the doc. Quick clarifications from Seastone security:

- Retention: Seastone policy requires 7 years for transaction-level logs and 3 years for aggregated analytics. Is Redwood able to guarantee 7-year retention for transactional logs in an EU region if we opt for EU residency?
- SIG/CAIQ: Tom will review the pre-filled CAIQ; if Redwood can provide the infra manifest (network diagrams, key rotation policy, KMS proofs) that would address the majority of open items.
- DPA: procurement would like to confirm that Redwood supports a carveout for data subject export obligations (we'll detail in redline).

We can do the evidence intake on 10/14 at 11:00am ET. Procurement also flagged a need for a short SOW paragraph we can attach to the MAP describing what Redwood will own vs Seastone for evidence collection and retention enforcement.

Anya
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Anya Novak <anya.novak@seastone.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-15T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security gate dependency grid and MAP sequencing — Seastone Financial evaluation

Anya, Tom, procurement team — great session today. Summary and next steps (formalizing into MAP draft attached):

1) Evidence intake (10/14 — complete) — CAIQ pre-fill reviewed. Outstanding infra artifacts: network diagram (Redwood infra), KMS rotation logs (Redwood), staging-access audit logs (Redwood + Seastone). Owners: Redwood (Kimberly), Seastone (Tom)
2) SOC 2 mapping (target: 10/29) — Redwood to provide control mappings for hosted evaluation and a short checklist for private deployment controls. Owner: Kimberly
3) DPA redlines (target: 11/05) — Redwood legal to accept most commercial redlines; data subject export clause flagged for joint language. Owner: Redwood legal + Seastone legal
4) Retention commitment: Redwood can support 7-year retention for transaction logs. If EU residency is required, we'll route storage to EU region (additional configuration fee may apply). Confirm requirement by 10/22.
5) Staging evaluation (hosted) — target start 11/02, acceptance window 11/02–11/12. Owners: Seastone QA (Anya) + Redwood solutions (Karthik)
6) Private cutover (if elected) — tentative start 11/16; dependent on DPA sign and infra runbook completion.

Attachments included: map-draft-seastone-2026-10-15.docx (draft MAP with milestone table), updated security-dependency-grid-v1.xlsx (owner-colors), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Immediate asks for Seastone to close on the MAP:
- Confirm EU residency requirement for transaction logs by 10/22
- Procurement: send draft DPA redline list (we'll deliver counterparty SOW language)

I'll open a HubSpot record for the MAP (link below) and create a short SOW paragraph draft for procurement to review. If we get the residency decision and DPA redlines on schedule, we can keep the MAP on the timeline above.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Manager, Solutions — Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Attachments: map-draft-seastone-2026-10-15.docx (docx), updated security-dependency-grid-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (pdf)
